answers.value: Universal liquid glass for 3D objects, TouchDesigner 2025.x, GLSL 4.60, macOS Apple Silicon.
Adjustable glass colour and reflection, translucency, opacity, overall glass style.
No dithering; continuous only. The shader never calls TDDither and uses mipmaps, not noise, for blur.
Menu that loads editable values, plus an A/B morph.
Separate Refraction and Reflection TOPs where the route uses them. This route uses only the Refraction TOP; reflections come from Environment Light COMPs.
TouchDesigner users new to GLSL.
Universality first, then match the four reference images (look, not shape).
Light COMPs via TDLightingPBR, Environment Light via TDEnvLightTextureLod/TDEnvLightingPBR, built-in fallback, compile for 0/1/3 lights and 0/1 env lights.
TDLightingPBR (GGX) rather than TDLighting (Phong): roughness ties highlight size and reflection blur to one PBR vocabulary.
Decided per kind: a scene with lights but no env light keeps its lights and uses the studio for reflections.
No back-face pass, Reflection TOP or flat-image reflection; Thickness slider only.
Same twelve names as the core; look values only (Shininess -> Highlight size, Reflection blur -> Reflection roughness, new Ambient); retuned by previews.

Warm point key at upper right (3, 3.5, 4), blue-violet point rim at the left side behind (-4, 1.5, -1.5), Environment Light on a coloured studio panorama. Chosen so the fallback (built-in key upper left) is visibly different.
studies/liquid-glass-lit/, self-contained; core read from commit a6f95c6 only.
Render Pass TOP on the scene render (depth kept) is the documented route; Over TOP only for flat image or video backgrounds. Reason: universality first (objects can pass in front of the glass).
demo_scene Render TOP draws the backdrop on a card at the far plane (card.vert/card.frag) so the demo follows the README recipe; the default image stays the same (captures within 1/255).
A dark grey bar at (0.55, 0, 1.6), off by default so the default look is unchanged; Study > Demo occluder turns it on.
apply() resets every control to its default first; Preset, Refraction TOP, Flip screen V and wired parameters are kept because they belong to the user's setup.
No change to Auto (the shader cannot tell a dimmed light from a missing one); a Demo Light COMP dimmer control, a native experiment and README advice instead.
Zero in every colour buffer after the first, as TouchDesigner's own exported PBR shader does.

Bring R1, R3, R4, R5, R6, R8, R9 and C1 to C9 from the core where they apply; keep lit's identity and its better solutions; record what does not apply (R7: no back-face pass) and what lit already had (R2, C4, C5).

answers.origin: supplied (family sync, from the user brief)
answers.value: No dithering anywhere: Dither off on both demo renders, README tells users to turn it off on theirs, a lint bans per-pixel noise in every shader.
The core's presets.advance()/phase()/spin(): wobble and film drift integrated in Python doubles, lattice wrapped at 256, no absTime in node expressions.

Setup controls kept: Refraction TOP, Faces, Object size, Flip screen V, Colour parameters. Scene-light settings stay reset, because experiment predictions depend on them. Lit's rule of skipping wired parameters is kept.

answers.topic: Fit to Glass geometry (labelled 'Fit to glass objects' before the family names fix)
answers.value: No Glass geometry field (the core has one for its back-face pass): Fit finds the Geometry COMPs that wear the material, preferring objects outside the component over the demo torus. Reason: least wiring.
Colour parameters decode the typed glass, reflection, rim and built-in key colours; scene light colours come from TouchDesigner unchanged.

Flip V flips the base UV and the measured vertical direction together, as the core does, instead of UV-only as the sync brief said: the core measured that UV-only breaks both Flip V cases once the direction is measured.

answers.origin: supplied (family sync: adopt only if the core did)
answers.value: Not adopted, because the core rejected it with measurements; lit's guard test gives the core's numbers exactly.
Kept lit's per-object Material on the glass Geometry COMPs; the README notes Override Material on the pass should work too (the core's form).
Study > Demo backdrop: Checker (default, unchanged) or Type; experiment type_backdrop; contact sheets on both.

Object size is the object's size in the world: the ripple and film frequencies are multiplied by the Geometry COMP's world scale (cube root of |det(world)|), so Fit's value reproduces a preset on a COMP-scaled object.

answers.topic: Family Object size rule: which meaning
answers.value: Choose one family rule and record it; the verifier noted that universality first (the user's priority) argues for lit's rule. Chosen: lit's V1 meaning (decisions.json, family_rule).

answers.topic: Family Object size rule: reference radius
answers.value: 1.45, the core's demo torus (radx 1 + rady 0.45, unscaled Geometry COMP), not Prism's 1.265: the core is the family's reference and lit already uses it, so lit's and the core's values agree on objects sized in their SOP.

answers.topic: Family Object size rule: what changes in lit
answers.value: No shader, uniform, Fit or preset change, so no capture changes. The rule is pinned by two unit tests (FamilyObjectSizeRule), including the 1.45 reference radius that nothing pinned before. The ports to the core, Prism and Flow are outside this study's write scope and stay pending there; the README's 'Object size across the family' tells users how the values differ until then.

answers.topic: Family Object size rule: parent transforms
answers.value: The rule counts the Geometry COMP's worldTransform. Derivative's ObjectCOMP Class page calls it 'the current world transform' and says localTransform leaves out parent transforms; that parents count is read from that contrast and added as a native check.

answers.topic: Screen orientation on the centre lines (C6 gap)
answers.value: Measure Prism's guarded derivative tie-break and Flow's two-pixel dead zone with Prism's screen_orientation_has_no_wrong_pixels on torus, knot and sphere at 480 x 270 and 481 x 271, adopt the better one, and record both findings (Flow's multisampled centre-column pixel, Prism's odd-size centre row).

answers.topic: Screen orientation on the centre lines: which form
answers.value: Prism's tie-break (decisions.json, last entry). The dead zone fails the flipped raster, the case the measurement exists for (about 340,000 wrong pixels in the sweep). Also measured and not taken: the tie-break over a two-pixel band (one new wrong single-sample pixel) and a centroid-sampled position (a second varying, untested in TouchDesigner). Both would fix more of the multisampled silhouette pixels; they are listed for the core to decide. The test asserts a residual bound (2 single-sample, 20 multisampled wrong pixels per row of twelve renders; 10 multisampled since the family critic's centre-line residual round) rather than zero, because both residuals are measured and explained.
Add the quarter-gap row to lit's C3 decision so the family record says why only Liquid Glass Blobs keeps it.

open_questions: Native check: does TDEnvLightTextureLod read a mipmapped map in 2025.x, and which way does Environment Map Rotate turn it?
Native check: relative brightness of TDLightingPBR diffuse/specular compared with the built-in key light.
Native check: does a Render Pass TOP that samples its input render warn about a cook dependency? Does the backdrop card show upright and fill the view?
Native check: do Light COMPs below Dimmer 0.001 leave TD_NUM_LIGHTS (experiment blackout)?
Native check: does the Environment Light's panorama wrap sideways at blurry mip levels (experiment env_seam), and do cube-map Environment Lights reflect?
Native check: does the Render Pick DAT pick the glass through the documented TD_PICKING_ACTIVE form, where a pick render runs only the placement and TDWritePickingValues() (family close G6)?

Native check: with linear fog at Fog Far 1, does the glass read fog colour x alpha plus the scene x (1 - alpha), with the demo backdrop unfogged? Does Fit to Glass geometry read the expected bounds, including 0.1 on a Geometry COMP scaled 0.1?
Taste: the re-seeded wobble and film patterns (family sync R1) look like the previous ones in kind; confirm they are acceptable.

Family (resolved in the family close, 2026-11-02): the core, Prism and Flow now follow the Object size rule; measured with each member's own Fit code (decisions.json, family_rule.members_family_close). Liquid Glass Blobs takes the rule's Object size number with two recorded exceptions: its film count is 2.5 per box radius, and its ripple follows the box, not Object size (Blobs decisions.json, 'Family close G1'; close verify LIT-CV3). Taste, still open: whether those two exceptions should stay once Blobs and a mesh member are seen side by side in TouchDesigner.

Family open question (centre-line residual): with antialiasing, a few silhouette pixels near the render's centre row or column still take the wrong screen orientation, so they bend the wrong way. In the WebGL preview each member's survey finds up to 8 of them per row of twelve renders; in the final image they change at most 7 pixels per row, by up to 43/255 in an emulated flipped raster and up to 38/255 in TouchDesigner's usual one. Are they visible in TouchDesigner? The native check centre_line_residual (validation.json, family_close.native_run) answers it. If they are, try a centroid-qualified vertex output for the projected position in Liquid Glass Lit first (form (e) of Lit's survey), then bring it to the core and the other members. Until then no member changes its shader for it.
Native check: in a TouchDesigner build, render the glass at an odd size (for example 481 x 271) with Flip screen V off; the centre row and column must bend like their neighbours.

Family critic: should Object size switch to SOP units, with the shader following the Geometry COMP's scale and each instance's scale by itself (decisions.json, Family critic: one Object size per component, option (b))? It would make animated and per-instance scale work without Fit, but changes what a typed Object size means on a scaled COMP, in every member.
